title.zh: 卷一百四十四 列傳第三十二 盛庸 平安 何福 顧成
title.en: Volume 144 Biographies 32: Cheng Yong, Ping An, He Fu, Gu Cheng
title.raw: 卷一百四十四 列傳第三十二 盛庸 平安 何福 顧成 Volume 144 Biographies 32: Cheng Yong, Ping An, He Fu, Gu Cheng

sentences.zh: 盛庸平安何福顧成

translations.literal: Sheng Yong, Ping An, He Fu, Gu Cheng
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Yong, Ping An, He Fu, and Gu Cheng

sentences.zh: 盛庸，不知何許人。

translations.literal: Sheng Yong—his place of origin is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Yong was a man of unknown origins.

sentences.zh: 洪武中，累官至都指揮。

translations.literal: During the Hongwu reign he rose through successive posts to Chief Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongwu he advanced through the ranks until he reached the post of Chief Commander.

sentences.zh: 建文初，以參將從耿炳文伐燕。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianwen reign, as a deputy general he followed Geng Bingwen in campaigning against Yan.
translations.idiomatic: When Jianwen took the throne, he served as a deputy general under Geng Bingwen in the expedition against the Prince of Yan.

sentences.zh: 李景隆代炳文，遂隸景隆麾下。

translations.literal: Li Jinglong replaced Bingwen, and he thereupon came under Jinglong's command.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jinglong replaced Geng Bingwen, Sheng Yong was transferred to Jinglong's command.

sentences.zh: 二年四月，景隆敗於白溝河，走濟南。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year, Jinglong was defeated at the Baigou River and fled to Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Jianwen 2 (1400), Jinglong was beaten at the Baigou River and retreated to Jinan.

sentences.zh: 燕師隨至，景隆復南走。

translations.literal: The Yan army followed in pursuit, and Jinglong again fled south.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan forces pursued, and Jinglong fled south once more.

sentences.zh: 庸與參政鐵鉉悉力固守，燕師攻圍三月不克。

translations.literal: Yong and the Administrator Tie Xian defended with all their strength; the Yan army besieged them for three months without taking the city.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Yong and the chief administrator Tie Xian held the city with all they had; the Yan army laid siege for three months and could not break in.

sentences.zh: 庸、鉉乘夜出兵掩擊，燕眾大敗，解圍去。

translations.literal: Yong and Xian led troops out by night in a surprise attack; the Yan forces were greatly defeated and lifted the siege and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Yong and Tie Xian stole out under cover of night and struck the Yan camp; the invaders were routed, and the siege was lifted.

sentences.zh: 乘勝復德州。

translations.literal: Riding the victory, they recovered Dezhou.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed their advantage and retook Dezhou.

sentences.zh: 九月，論功封歷城侯，祿千石。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, for merit he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Licheng with an income of one thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: That September he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Licheng, with a stipend of one thousand piculs of grain.

sentences.zh: 尋命為平燕將軍，充總兵官。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was appointed General for the Pacification of Yan and made overall commander.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was named General for the Pacification of Yan and placed in supreme command of the army.

sentences.zh: 陳暉、平安為左右副總兵，馬溥、徐真為左右參將，進鉉兵部尚書參贊軍務。

translations.literal: Chen Hui and Ping An were made left and right deputy commanders-in-chief; Ma Pu and Xu Zhen were made left and right assistant generals; Xian was promoted to Minister of War to assist in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Hui and Ping An became his deputies, Ma Pu and Xu Zhen his wing commanders, and Tie Xian was promoted to Minister of War to advise on strategy.

sentences.zh: 時吳傑、平安守定州，庸駐德州，徐凱屯滄州，為犄角。

translations.literal: At that time Wu Jie and Ping An held Dingzhou, Yong was stationed at Dezhou, and Xu Kai garrisoned Cangzhou, forming a pincer.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Jie and Ping An held Dingzhou, Yong kept Dezhou, and Xu Kai was posted at Cangzhou, the three positions forming a mutual defense.

sentences.zh: 是冬，燕兵襲滄州，破，擒凱。

translations.literal: That winter the Yan army raided Cangzhou, defeated the garrison, and captured Kai.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the Yan forces struck Cangzhou, broke the defense, and took Xu Kai prisoner.

sentences.zh: 掠其輜重，進薄濟寧。

translations.literal: They plundered the baggage train and pressed forward toward Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: They seized the supply train and advanced on Jinan.

sentences.zh: 庸引兵屯東昌以邀之，背城而陣。

translations.literal: Yong led his army to encamp at Dongchang to intercept them and drew up battle lines with the city at his back.
translations.idiomatic: Yong moved his troops to Dongchang to block their path and formed his battle line with the city behind him.

sentences.zh: 燕王帥兵直前薄庸軍左翼，不動。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yan led his troops straight forward to press Yong's left wing, which did not stir.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yan drove his men straight at Yong's left wing, but the line held firm.

sentences.zh: 復沖中堅，庸開陣縱王入，圍之數重。

translations.literal: He again charged the center; Yong opened his formation and let the Prince enter, then surrounded him in many rings.
translations.idiomatic: The prince charged again at the center; Yong deliberately opened a gap, let him in, and closed ranks around him in layer upon layer.

sentences.zh: 燕將朱能帥番騎來救，王乘間突圍出。

translations.literal: The Yan general Zhu Neng led barbarian cavalry to the rescue, and the Prince seized an opening and broke out of the encirclement.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Neng led allied cavalry to the rescue, and the prince found a gap and fought his way out.

sentences.zh: 而燕軍為火器所傷甚眾，大將張玉死於陣。

translations.literal: But the Yan army suffered heavily from firearms; the great general Zhang Yu died in the battle line.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan army, however, took heavy losses from gunpowder weapons, and their great commander Zhang Yu was killed in the field.

sentences.zh: 王獨以百騎殿，退至館陶。

translations.literal: The Prince alone with a hundred cavalry brought up the rear and withdrew to Guantao.
translations.idiomatic: The prince himself covered the retreat with a hundred horsemen and fell back to Guantao.

sentences.zh: 庸檄吳傑、平安自真定遮燕歸路。

translations.literal: Yong dispatched orders to Wu Jie and Ping An from Zhending to block the Yan army's line of retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Yong sent word to Wu Jie and Ping An at Zhending to cut off the Yan army's withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，傑、平安戰深州不利，燕師始得歸。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year Jie and Ping An fought at Shenzhou without success, and only then could the Yan army return home.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, in the first month, Wu Jie and Ping An were defeated at Shenzhou, and only then were the Yan forces able to get home.

sentences.zh: 是役也，燕精銳喪失幾盡，庸軍聲大振，帝為享廟告捷。

translations.literal: In this campaign the elite troops of Yan were almost entirely lost; Yong's army's reputation rose greatly, and the Emperor offered sacrifice at the ancestral temple to announce the victory.
translations.idiomatic: In that battle the Yan army's best troops were nearly wiped out; Yong's fame soared, and the emperor held a temple offering to proclaim triumph.

sentences.zh: 三月，燕兵復南出保定。

translations.literal: In the third month the Yan army again marched south from Baoding.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the Yan forces marched south again from Baoding.

sentences.zh: 庸營夾河。

translations.literal: Yong encamped along the Jia River.
translations.idiomatic: Yong pitched his camp on the banks of the Jia River.

sentences.zh: 王將輕騎來覘，掠陣而過。

translations.literal: The Prince led light cavalry to reconnoiter, skimming past the battle line.
translations.idiomatic: The prince rode out with light cavalry to scout the enemy lines, sweeping past them in a feint.

sentences.zh: 庸遣千騎追之，為燕兵射卻。

translations.literal: Yong sent a thousand cavalry in pursuit, but they were driven back by Yan archery.
translations.idiomatic: Yong sent a thousand horsemen after him, but Yan archers drove them off.

sentences.zh: 及戰，庸軍列盾以進。

translations.literal: When battle was joined, Yong's army advanced in shield formation.
translations.idiomatic: When the armies clashed, Yong's troops advanced behind a wall of shields.

sentences.zh: 王令步卒先攻，騎兵乘間馳入。

translations.literal: The Prince ordered the infantry to attack first, and the cavalry seized openings and galloped in.
translations.idiomatic: The prince sent his foot soldiers forward first, then sent his cavalry charging through the gaps.

sentences.zh: 庸麾軍力戰，斬其將譚淵。

translations.literal: Yong commanded his army to fight desperately and slew the Yan general Tan Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yong rallied his men for a bitter fight and killed the Yan general Tan Yuan.

sentences.zh: 而朱能、張武等帥眾殊死鬥。

translations.literal: But Zhu Neng, Zhang Wu, and others led their troops in a death struggle.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Neng, Zhang Wu, and others, however, led their men in a desperate counterattack.

sentences.zh: 王以勁騎貫陣與能合。

translations.literal: The Prince with crack cavalry pierced through the battle line to join Neng.
translations.idiomatic: The prince broke through with elite horsemen and linked up with Zhu Neng.

sentences.zh: 庸部驍將莊得、皂旗張等俱戰死。

translations.literal: Yong's fierce generals Zhuang De, Zhang of the Black Banner, and others all died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Among Yong's champions, Zhuang De, Zhang of the Black Banner, and others were all killed.

sentences.zh: 是日，燕軍幾敗。

translations.literal: That day the Yan army nearly suffered defeat.
translations.idiomatic: That day the Yan army came close to ruin.

sentences.zh: 明日復戰，燕軍東北，庸軍西南，自辰至未，互勝負。

translations.literal: The next day they fought again: the Yan army on the northeast, Yong's army on the southwest; from the seventh to the second hour of the afternoon, victory seesawed.
translations.idiomatic: They fought again the next day, the Yan force to the northeast and Yong's to the southwest; from morning until mid-afternoon neither side could gain the upper hand.

sentences.zh: 兩軍皆疲，將士各坐息。

translations.literal: Both armies were exhausted, and officers and men all sat down to rest.
translations.idiomatic: Both armies were spent, and the soldiers on both sides sank down where they stood to catch their breath.

sentences.zh: 復起戰，忽東北風大起，飛塵蔽天。

translations.literal: They rose again to fight, when suddenly a strong northeast wind arose and flying dust blotted out the sky.
translations.idiomatic: They went at each other once more, when a fierce northeast wind sprang up and whirling dust blotted out the sky.

sentences.zh: 燕兵乘風大呼，左右橫擊。

translations.literal: The Yan army rode the wind with great shouts and struck from both flanks.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan troops used the wind, roared their battle cries, and struck from both sides.

sentences.zh: 庸大敗走還德州，自是氣沮。

translations.literal: Yong was utterly defeated and fled back to Dezhou; from then on his spirits were crushed.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was routed and fled back to Dezhou; from that day his army lost heart.

sentences.zh: 已而燕將李遠焚糧艘於沛縣，庸軍遂乏餉。

translations.literal: Before long the Yan general Li Yuan burned grain ships at Peixian, and Yong's army thus lacked provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the Yan general Li Yuan burned the supply fleet at Pei County, and Yong's troops were left without rations.

sentences.zh: 明年，靈璧戰敗，平安等被執。

translations.literal: The next year, defeated at Lingbi, Ping An and others were captured.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, after the defeat at Lingbi, Ping An and the others were taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 庸獨引軍而南，列戰艦淮南岸。

translations.literal: Yong alone led his army south and arrayed warships along the south bank of the Huai River.
translations.idiomatic: Yong alone marched south with his army and lined his war junks along the south bank of the Huai.

sentences.zh: 燕將邱福等潛濟，出庸後。

translations.literal: The Yan generals Qiu Fu and others crossed secretly and came out behind Yong.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan generals Qiu Fu and others forded in secret and got in behind Yong's position.

sentences.zh: 庸不能支，退為守江計。

translations.literal: Yong could not hold out and withdrew to plan for defending the river.
translations.idiomatic: Yong could not hold his ground and pulled back to mount a defense of the Yangzi line.

sentences.zh: 燕兵渡淮，由盱眙陷揚州。

translations.literal: The Yan army crossed the Huai, took Yangzhou by way of Xuyi.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan forces crossed the Huai, marched through Xuyi, and captured Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 庸禦戰於六合及浦子口，皆失利，都督陳瑄帥舟師降燕，燕兵遂渡江。

translations.literal: Yong resisted at Liuhe and Puzikou but was defeated at both; the Commissioner-in-chief Chen Xuan led the fleet in surrender to Yan, and the Yan army then crossed the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: Yong fought them at Liuhe and at Puzikou and lost both times; Chen Xuan, commander of the fleet, defected to Yan, and the Yan army crossed the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 庸倉卒聚海艘出高資港迎戰，復敗，軍益潰散。

translations.literal: Yong in haste gathered sea-going vessels and sailed out from Gaozi Harbor to give battle, was again defeated, and his army scattered further.
translations.idiomatic: Yong hastily gathered what sea vessels he could and sailed out of Gaozi Harbor to meet them; he was beaten again, and his army broke apart.

sentences.zh: 平安，滁人，小字保兒。

translations.literal: Ping An, a native of Chuzhou, his childhood name Baor.
translations.idiomatic: Ping An was a native of Chuzhou; his childhood name was Baor.

sentences.zh: 父定，從太祖起兵，官濟寧衛指揮僉事。

translations.literal: His father Ding followed the founding emperor in raising troops and served as Assistant Commander of the Jining Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ding had followed the founding emperor in the uprising and held the post of assistant commander of the Jining Guard.

sentences.zh: 從常遇春下元都，戰沒。

translations.literal: He followed Chang Yuchun in taking the Yuan capital and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: He marched with Chang Yuchun against the Yuan capital and was killed in action.

sentences.zh: 安初為太祖養子，驍勇善戰，力舉數百斤。

translations.literal: An was at first the founding emperor's adopted son; fierce and skilled in battle, he could lift several hundred jin.
translations.idiomatic: Ping An had first been the founding emperor's adopted son; he was a fierce fighter who could lift weights of several hundred jin.

sentences.zh: 襲父職，遷密雲指揮使，進右軍都督僉事。

translations.literal: He inherited his father's post, was transferred to Commander of Miyun, and advanced to Vice Commissioner-in-chief of the Right Army.
translations.idiomatic: He succeeded to his father's office, was posted as commander at Miyun, and rose to vice commissioner-in-chief of the Right Army.

sentences.zh: 燕兵圍濟南。

translations.literal: The Yan army besieged Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan army laid siege to Jinan.

sentences.zh: 安營單家橋，謀出御河奪燕餉舟。

translations.literal: An encamped at Danjia Bridge and planned to emerge on the Imperial Canal to seize Yan supply boats.
translations.idiomatic: Ping An encamped at Danjia Bridge and planned a sortie along the Grand Canal to seize the Yan supply fleet.

sentences.zh: 又選善水卒五千人渡河，將攻德州。

translations.literal: He also selected five thousand skilled water soldiers to cross the river and was about to attack Dezhou.
translations.idiomatic: He also picked five thousand seasoned river troops, crossed the river, and prepared to strike at Dezhou.

sentences.zh: 圍乃解。

translations.literal: The siege was then lifted.
translations.idiomatic: The siege was lifted.

sentences.zh: 安與吳傑進屯定州。

translations.literal: An and Wu Jie advanced to garrison Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ping An and Wu Jie moved up and encamped at Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，燕敗盛庸於夾河，回軍與安戰單家橋。

translations.literal: The next year Yan defeated Sheng Yong at the Jia River, turned his army about, and fought An at Danjia Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, after defeating Sheng Yong at the Jia River, the Yan army turned back and fought Ping An at Danjia Bridge.

sentences.zh: 安奮擊大破之，擒其將薛祿。

translations.literal: An fought fiercely and routed them utterly, capturing the Yan general Xue Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Ping An struck hard, routed them completely, and took the Yan general Xue Lu prisoner.

sentences.zh: 無何，逸去。

translations.literal: Before long he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Xue Lu escaped.

sentences.zh: 再戰滹沱河，又破之。

translations.literal: They fought again at the Hutuo River and he again defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: They clashed again on the Hutuo River, and Ping An routed them once more.

sentences.zh: 安於陣中縛木為樓，高數丈，戰酣，輒登樓望，發強弩射燕軍，死者甚眾。

translations.literal: An bound timbers into a tower in the battle line several zhang high; when the fighting grew hot he would climb the tower to look out and loose powerful crossbows at the Yan army, and very many were killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the field Ping An had a wooden tower several zhang high erected; when the fighting grew fierce he would climb it to survey the field and loose heavy crossbows at the Yan ranks, killing a great many.

sentences.zh: 忽大風起，發屋拔樹，聲如雷。

translations.literal: Suddenly a great wind arose, tearing off roofs and uprooting trees, with a sound like thunder.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly a violent wind sprang up, tearing off roofs and uprooting trees with a roar like thunder.

sentences.zh: 都指揮鄧戩、陳鵬等陷敵中，安遂敗走真定。

translations.literal: Chief Commanders Deng Jian and Chen Peng and others were trapped in the enemy ranks, and An thereupon was defeated and fled to Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: Chief commanders Deng Jian and Chen Peng and others were cut off in the enemy lines, and Ping An was driven back to Zhending.

sentences.zh: 燕王與南軍數大戰，每親身陷陣，所向皆靡，惟安與庸二軍屢挫之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yan fought many great battles with the southern army, each time plunging into the lines in person; wherever he went none could stand, yet only An's and Yong's two armies repeatedly checked him.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yan fought the southern forces again and again, always leading the charge in person and sweeping all before him—yet only Ping An's and Sheng Yong's armies repeatedly turned him back.

sentences.zh: 滹沱之戰，矢集王旗如蝟毛。

translations.literal: At the battle of the Hutuo, arrows clustered on the Prince's banner like hedgehog quills.
translations.idiomatic: At the Hutuo River the prince's standard bristled with arrows like a hedgehog's quills.

sentences.zh: 王使人送旗北平，諭世子謹藏，以示後世。

translations.literal: The Prince sent someone to deliver the banner to Beiping, instructing the heir to keep it carefully as a lesson for posterity.
translations.idiomatic: The prince sent the banner to Beiping and told his heir to preserve it carefully as a memorial for future generations.

sentences.zh: 顧成已先被執在燕，見而泣曰：「臣自少從軍，今老矣，多歷戰陣，未嘗見若此也。」

translations.literal: Gu Cheng had already been captured and was with the Yan forces; seeing it he wept and said, "I have followed the army since youth; now I am old and have seen many battle lines, yet never anything like this."
translations.idiomatic: Gu Cheng, already a prisoner with the Yan army, wept when he saw it and said, "I have soldiered since I was young; I am old now and have seen many battles, but never anything like this."

sentences.zh: 逾月，燕師出大名。

translations.literal: After more than a month the Yan army marched out from Daming.
translations.idiomatic: A month later the Yan army marched out from Daming.

sentences.zh: 安與庸及吳傑等分兵擾其餉道。

translations.literal: An, Yong, Wu Jie, and others divided their forces to harass his supply routes.
translations.idiomatic: Ping An, Sheng Yong, Wu Jie, and others split their forces to raid his supply lines.

sentences.zh: 燕王患之，遣指揮武勝上書於朝，請撤安等息兵，為緩師計。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yan was troubled by this and sent the commander Wu Sheng to submit a memorial to the court asking that An and the others be withdrawn and fighting cease, as a stratagem to slow the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: The prince, worried by these raids, sent Commander Wu Sheng to petition the court to recall Ping An and the others and halt hostilities—a ruse to buy time.

sentences.zh: 帝不許。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 燕王亦決計南下。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yan also resolved to march south.
translations.idiomatic: The prince resolved to march south in any case.

sentences.zh: 遣李遠等潛走沛縣，焚糧舟，掠彰德，破尾尖寨，諭降林縣。

translations.literal: He sent Li Yuan and others to slip secretly to Peixian, burn grain boats, plunder Zhangde, take Weijian Stockade, and induce Lin County to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Li Yuan and others secretly to Pei County to burn the grain fleet, raided Zhangde, stormed Weijian Stockade, and induced Lin County to submit.

sentences.zh: 時安在真定，度北平空虛，帥萬騎直走北平。

translations.literal: At that time An was at Zhending; judging Beiping empty, he led ten thousand cavalry straight for Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: Ping An was then at Zhending; judging Beiping undefended, he led ten thousand horsemen straight for the city.

sentences.zh: 至平村，去城五十里而軍。

translations.literal: He reached Pingcun and encamped fifty li from the city.
translations.idiomatic: He reached Pingcun and pitched camp fifty li from the city.

sentences.zh: 燕王懼，遣劉江等馳還救。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yan was alarmed and sent Liu Jiang and others galloping back to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: The prince was alarmed and sent Liu Jiang and others racing back to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 安戰不利，引還。

translations.literal: An fought without success and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Ping An was beaten and pulled back.

sentences.zh: 時大同守將房昭引兵入紫荊關，據易州西水寨以窺北平，安自真定餉之。

translations.literal: At that time Fang Zhao, garrison commander of Datong, led troops through Zijing Pass, held the West Water Stockade at Yizhou to threaten Beiping, and An supplied him from Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Fang Zhao, the Datong garrison commander, marched through Zijing Pass and held the West Water Stockade at Yizhou to threaten Beiping; Ping An supplied him from Zhending.

sentences.zh: 八月，燕兵北歸。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the Yan army returned north.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the Yan army marched north again.

sentences.zh: 安及燕將李彬戰於楊村，敗之。

translations.literal: An fought the Yan general Li Bin at Yangcun and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Ping An fought the Yan general Li Bin at Yangcun and routed him.

sentences.zh: 四年，燕兵復南下，破蕭縣。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the Yan army again marched south and took Xiaoxian.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the war the Yan forces marched south again and captured Xiaoxian.

sentences.zh: 安引軍躡其後，至淝河。

translations.literal: An led his army in pursuit to the Fei River.
translations.idiomatic: Ping An followed in pursuit as far as the Fei River.

sentences.zh: 燕將白義、王真、劉江迎敵。

translations.literal: The Yan generals Bai Yi, Wang Zhen, and Liu Jiang met him in battle.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan generals Bai Yi, Wang Zhen, and Liu Jiang came out to meet him.

sentences.zh: 安轉戰，斬真。

translations.literal: An fought in a wheeling engagement and slew Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: In the swirling fight Ping An killed Wang Zhen.

sentences.zh: 真，驍將。

translations.literal: Zhen was a fierce general.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhen had been one of the prince's boldest commanders.

sentences.zh: 燕王嘗曰：「諸將奮勇如王真，何事不成！

translations.literal: The Prince of Yan had once said, "If all my generals fought as fiercely as Wang Zhen, what could we not accomplish!
translations.idiomatic: The prince had once said, "If all my generals fought as fiercely as Wang Zhen, what could we not accomplish!

sentences.zh: 」至是為安所殺。

translations.literal: " Now he was killed by An.
translations.idiomatic: " Now Wang Zhen was killed by Ping An.

sentences.zh: 燕王乃身自迎戰，安部將火耳灰挺槊大呼，直前刺王。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yan thereupon met the enemy in person; An's subordinate general Huo'erhui levelled his spear, shouted, and charged straight forward to stab the Prince.
translations.idiomatic: The prince came out to fight in person; Ping An's officer Huo'erhui levelled his spear, roared, and charged straight at the prince.

sentences.zh: 馬忽蹶，被擒。

translations.literal: His horse suddenly stumbled, and he was captured.
translations.idiomatic: His horse stumbled suddenly and he was taken.

sentences.zh: 安稍引卻。

translations.literal: An drew back slightly.
translations.idiomatic: Ping An drew his line back a little.

sentences.zh: 已，復進至小河，張左右翼擊燕軍，斬其將陳文。

translations.literal: Before long he again advanced to the Xiao River, deployed his left and right wings to strike the Yan army, and slew the Yan general Chen Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he advanced again to the Xiao River, sent his wings against the Yan army, and killed the Yan general Chen Wen.

sentences.zh: 已，復移軍齊眉山，與諸將列陣大戰。

translations.literal: Before long he again shifted his army to Qimei Mountain and with the other generals drew up battle lines for a great fight.
translations.idiomatic: He then moved his army to Qimei Mountain and, with the other commanders, formed battle lines for a major engagement.

sentences.zh: 自午至酉，又敗之。

translations.literal: From noon to the second hour of the evening he again defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: From midday until evening he routed them again.

sentences.zh: 燕諸將謀北還，圖後舉。

translations.literal: The Yan generals planned to return north and try again later.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan generals urged a retreat to the north and a fresh attempt later.

sentences.zh: 王不聽。

translations.literal: The Prince would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The prince would not hear of it.

sentences.zh: 尋阻何福軍亦至，與安合。

translations.literal: Before long He Fu's army, which had been blocking the way, also arrived and joined An.
translations.idiomatic: Soon He Fu's army, which had been holding the line of advance, arrived and joined Ping An.

sentences.zh: 燕軍益大懼，王晝夜擐甲者數日。

translations.literal: The Yan army grew still more fearful; for several days the Prince wore armor day and night.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan army was more alarmed than ever; for several days the prince wore his armor day and night.

sentences.zh: 福欲持久老燕師，移營靈璧，深塹高壘自固。

translations.literal: Fu wished to wear down the Yan army in a prolonged campaign; he moved camp to Lingbi and dug deep moats and raised high ramparts to secure himself.
translations.idiomatic: He Fu planned to wear the Yan army down in a war of attrition, shifted camp to Lingbi, and dug deep trenches and high ramparts to hold his ground.

sentences.zh: 而糧運為燕兵所陰，不得達。

translations.literal: But grain transport was secretly intercepted by the Yan army and could not get through.
translations.idiomatic: Yan forces cut off his grain supply in secret, and no provisions could reach the camp.

sentences.zh: 安分兵往迎，燕王以精騎遮安軍，分為二。

translations.literal: An divided his forces to go meet the convoy; the Prince of Yan with elite cavalry intercepted An's army and split it in two.
translations.idiomatic: Ping An sent troops to escort the supplies; the prince intercepted them with elite cavalry and cut Ping An's force in two.

sentences.zh: 福開壁來援，為高煦所敗。

translations.literal: Fu opened the stockade to come to the rescue and was defeated by Gao Xu.
translations.idiomatic: He Fu marched out of the camp to relieve them and was beaten by Gao Xu.

sentences.zh: 諸將謀移軍淮河就糧，夜令軍中聞三炮即走。

translations.literal: The generals planned to move the army to the Huai River for grain and ordered that at night, on hearing three cannon shots, the troops were to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: The generals decided to move toward the Huai for supplies and gave orders that three cannon shots at night would be the signal to retreat.

sentences.zh: 翌日，燕軍猝薄壘，發三炮。

translations.literal: The next day the Yan army suddenly pressed the ramparts and fired three cannon shots.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the Yan army rushed the ramparts and fired three cannon shots.

sentences.zh: 軍中誤以為己號，爭趨門，遂大亂。

translations.literal: The army mistook this for their own signal and all rushed for the gates, whereupon great disorder ensued.
translations.idiomatic: The southern troops took it for their own signal and surged for the gates in panic.

sentences.zh: 燕兵乘之，人馬墜壕塹俱滿。

translations.literal: The Yan army seized the opportunity; men and horses falling into moats and ditches filled them completely.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan army pressed the rout; men and horses filled the ditches and moats as they fell.

sentences.zh: 福單騎走，安及陳暉、馬溥、徐真、孫成等三十七人皆被執。

translations.literal: Fu fled alone on horseback; An and Chen Hui, Ma Pu, Xu Zhen, Sun Cheng, and thirty-seven others were all captured.
translations.idiomatic: He Fu fled alone on horseback; Ping An, Chen Hui, Ma Pu, Xu Zhen, Sun Cheng, and thirty-seven others were taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 文臣宦官在軍被執者又百五十余人，時四月辛巳也。

translations.literal: Civil officials and eunuchs with the army who were captured numbered more than one hundred fifty besides; the day was xinsi in the fourth month.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred and fifty civil officials and eunuchs with the army were also captured; the day was xinsi in the fourth month.

sentences.zh: 安久駐真定，屢敗燕兵，斬驍將數人，燕將莫敢嬰其鋒。

translations.literal: An had long been stationed at Zhending, repeatedly defeating the Yan army and slaying several fierce generals; no Yan general dared meet his edge.
translations.idiomatic: Ping An had long held Zhending, repeatedly beating the Yan army and killing several of their boldest commanders; no Yan officer dared face him head-on.

sentences.zh: 至是被擒，軍中歡呼動地，曰：「吾屬自此獲安矣！

translations.literal: When at last he was captured, the army shouted until heaven and earth shook, saying, "From now on we shall have peace!
translations.idiomatic: When he was finally taken, the Yan camp erupted in cheers: "From now on we shall have peace!

sentences.zh: 」爭請殺安。

translations.literal: " All vied to ask that An be killed.
translations.idiomatic: " Men clamored to have Ping An executed.

sentences.zh: 燕王惜其材勇，選銳卒衛送北平，命世子及郭資等善視之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yan valued his talent and courage, selected crack troops to escort him to Beiping, and ordered the heir and Guo Zi and others to treat him well.
translations.idiomatic: The prince prized his ability and courage, sent elite guards to escort him to Beiping, and told the heir and Guo Zi and others to treat him well.

sentences.zh: 王即帝位，以安為北平都指揮使。

translations.literal: When the Prince took the throne, he appointed An Chief Commander of Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince became emperor, he made Ping An chief commander of Beiping.

sentences.zh: 尋進行後府都督僉事。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was advanced to Vice Commissioner-in-chief of the Rear Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was promoted to vice commissioner-in-chief of the Rear Palace.

sentences.zh: 永樂七年三月，帝巡北京。

translations.literal: In the third month of the seventh year of Yongle the Emperor toured Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Yongle 7 the emperor toured Beiping.

sentences.zh: 將至，覽章奏見安名，謂左右曰：「平保兒尚在耶？

translations.literal: As he was about to arrive, reviewing memorials he saw An's name and said to those beside him, "Is Ping Baor still alive?
translations.idiomatic: On the way he read through memorials, saw Ping An's name, and said to his attendants, "Is Ping Baor still alive?

sentences.zh: 」安聞之，遂自殺。

translations.literal: " When An heard of it he thereupon killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: " When Ping An heard of it, he took his own life.

sentences.zh: 命以指揮使祿給其子。

translations.literal: He ordered that a commander's stipend be given to his son.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered that his son receive a commander's stipend.

sentences.zh: 何福，鳳陽人。

translations.literal: He Fu, a native of Fengyang.
translations.idiomatic: He Fu was a native of Fengyang.

sentences.zh: 洪武初，累功為金吾後衛指揮同知。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Hongwu, through accumulated merit he became Vice Commander of the Rear Jinwu Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Hongwu reign he rose through merit to vice commander of the Rear Jinwu Guard.

sentences.zh: 從傅友德征雲南，擢都督僉事。

translations.literal: He followed Fu Youde in the Yunnan campaign and was promoted to Vice Commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He marched with Fu Youde against Yunnan and was promoted to vice commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 又從藍玉出塞，至捕魚兒海。

translations.literal: He again followed Lan Yu beyond the frontier to Buyur Lake.
translations.idiomatic: He also followed Lan Yu beyond the frontier as far as Buyur Lake.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，江陰侯吳高帥迤北降人南征。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year Marquis of Jiangyin Wu Gao led surrendered northerners on a southern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year Marquis of Jiangyin Wu Gao led surrendered northerners on a campaign south.

sentences.zh: 抵沅江，眾叛，由思州出荊、樊，道渭河，欲遁歸沙漠。

translations.literal: Reaching the Yuan River, the host rebelled; they went out through Sizhou toward Jing and Fan, took the Wei River route, and wished to escape back to the desert.
translations.idiomatic: At the Yuan River the troops mutinied; they broke out through Sizhou toward Jing and Fan, followed the Wei River route, and tried to flee back to the steppe.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，福與都督聶緯追擊，及諸鹿阝、延，盡殲之。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year Fu and Vice Commissioner Nie Wei pursued them, caught them at Zhulu and Yan, and annihilated them completely.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, in the first month, He Fu and Vice Commissioner Nie Wei pursued them, caught them at Zhulu and Yan, and wiped them out.

sentences.zh: 移兵討平都勻蠻，俘斬萬計。

translations.literal: He shifted troops to pacify the Duyun tribes, capturing and killing on the order of ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He then moved against the Duyun tribes and killed or captured tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，拜平羌將軍，討越州叛蠻阿資，破降之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was appointed General for the Pacification of the Qiang and campaigned against the rebel tribesman Azi of Yuezhou, defeating and accepting his surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he was named General for the Pacification of the Qiang, defeated the rebel chieftain Azi of Yuezhou, and accepted his surrender.

sentences.zh: 擇地立柵處其眾，置寧越堡。

translations.literal: He chose ground, set up stockades to settle their people, and established Ningyue Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: He chose a site, built stockades for the surrendered people, and established Ningyue Stockade.

sentences.zh: 遂平九名、九姓諸蠻。

translations.literal: He thereupon pacified the Jiuming and Jiuxing tribes and others.
translations.idiomatic: He then pacified the Jiuming, Jiuxing, and other tribal groups.

sentences.zh: 尋與都督茅鼎會兵，徇五開。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he joined Vice Commissioner Mao Ding's forces to advance on Wukai.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he joined Vice Commissioner Mao Ding and marched on Wukai.

sentences.zh: 未行，而畢節諸蠻復叛，大掠屯堡，殺吏士。

translations.literal: Before they set out, the Bijie tribes rebelled again, raiding garrison posts on a great scale and killing officials and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Before they could march, the Bijie tribes rebelled again, sacked garrison posts, and killed officials and troops.

sentences.zh: 福令畢節諸衛嚴備，而檄都督陶文等從鼎搗其巢。

translations.literal: Fu ordered the Bijie guards to stand on strict alert and dispatched orders to Vice Commissioner Tao Wen and others to follow Ding in striking their lair.
translations.idiomatic: He Fu ordered the Bijie guards to stand ready and sent Vice Commissioner Tao Wen and others with Mao Ding to strike their stronghold.

sentences.zh: 擒叛酋，戮之。

translations.literal: They captured the rebel chieftain and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: They captured the rebel leader and executed him.

sentences.zh: 分兵盡捕諸蠻，建堡設戍，乃趨五開。

translations.literal: They divided forces to capture all the tribes, built stockades and set garrisons, and then pressed on to Wukai.
translations.idiomatic: They split their forces to round up the tribes, built stockades and garrisons, and then advanced on Wukai.

sentences.zh: 請因兵力討水西奢香，不許。

translations.literal: He requested to use his army's strength to campaign against She Xiang of Shuixi; permission was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to use his troops against She Xiang of Shuixi, but the court refused.

sentences.zh: 三十年三月，水西蠻居宗必登等作亂，會顧成討平之。

translations.literal: In the third month of the thirtieth year the Shuixi tribesman Juzong Bideng and others rebelled; Gu Cheng happened to campaign and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the thirtieth year the Shuixi chieftain Juzong Bideng and others rose in revolt; Gu Cheng happened to be campaigning there and put them down.

sentences.zh: 其冬拜征虜左將軍，副西平侯沐春討麓川叛蠻刀幹孟。

translations.literal: That winter he was appointed Left General for the Punishment of Barbarians and served as deputy to Marquis of Xiping Mu Chun in campaigning against the Luchuan rebel tribesman Dao Ganmeng.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was named Left General for the Punishment of Barbarians and served under Marquis of Xiping Mu Chun against the Luchuan rebel Dao Ganmeng.

sentences.zh: 明年，福與都督瞿能逾高良公山，搗南甸，擒其酋刀名孟。

translations.literal: The next year Fu and Vice Commissioner Qu Neng crossed Gaolianggong Mountain, struck Nandian, and captured the chieftain Dao Mingmeng.
translations.idiomatic: The next year He Fu and Vice Commissioner Qu Neng crossed Gaolianggong Mountain, struck Nandian, and captured the chieftain Dao Mingmeng.

sentences.zh: 回軍擊景罕寨，不下。

translations.literal: On the return march they attacked Jinghan Stockade but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: On the return march they attacked Jinghan Stockade but could not take it.

sentences.zh: 春以銳軍至，賊驚潰。

translations.literal: Chun arrived with crack troops and the rebels fled in panic.
translations.idiomatic: Mu Chun arrived with elite troops and the rebels broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 幹孟懼，乞降。

translations.literal: Ganmeng was afraid and begged to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Dao Ganmeng was terrified and sued for peace.

sentences.zh: 已而春卒，賊復懷貳。

translations.literal: Before long Chun died, and the rebels again harbored double loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Mu Chun died, and the rebels wavered in their submission again.

sentences.zh: 是時太祖已崩，惠帝初即位，拜福征虜將軍。

translations.literal: At that time the founding emperor had died and the Huandi had just taken the throne; Fu was appointed General for the Punishment of Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: By then the founding emperor was dead and the new emperor had just taken the throne; He Fu was appointed General for the Punishment of Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 福遂破擒刀幹孟，降其眾七萬。

translations.literal: Fu thereupon defeated and captured Dao Ganmeng and received the surrender of seventy thousand of his followers.
translations.idiomatic: He Fu then defeated and captured Dao Ganmeng and accepted the surrender of seventy thousand of his followers.

sentences.zh: 分兵徇下諸寨，麓川地悉定。

translations.literal: He divided forces to subdue the stockades below, and the Luchuan region was entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: He sent detachments to subdue the outlying stockades, and the whole Luchuan region was pacified.

sentences.zh: 建文元年，還京師，論功進都督同知。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianwen he returned to the capital; for merit he was advanced to Vice Commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianwen 1 he returned to the capital and was promoted to vice commissioner-in-chief for his service.

sentences.zh: 練兵德州，進左都督。

translations.literal: He trained troops at Dezhou and was advanced to Left Commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He drilled troops at Dezhou and was promoted to left commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 與盛庸、平安會兵伐燕，戰淮北不利，奔還。

translations.literal: He joined Sheng Yong and Ping An in campaigning against Yan; fighting north of the Huai without success, he fled back.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Sheng Yong and Ping An against the Prince of Yan; beaten north of the Huai, he fled back.

sentences.zh: 成祖即位，以福宿將知兵，推誠用之。

translations.literal: When Chengzu took the throne, because Fu was a veteran who understood warfare, he employed him with full trust.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yongle Emperor took the throne, he trusted He Fu—a veteran who knew war—and used him with complete confidence.

sentences.zh: 聘其甥女徐氏為趙王妃。

translations.literal: He betrothed Fu's niece, the Xu clan, as Princess of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: He betrothed Fu's niece of the Xu clan to the Prince of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 尋，命佩征虜將軍印，充總兵官，鎮寧夏，節制山、陜、河南諸軍。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was ordered to wear the seal of General for the Punishment of Barbarians, serve as overall commander, garrison Ningxia, and control the armies of Shanxi, Shaanxi, and Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was given the seal of General for the Punishment of Barbarians, made supreme commander at Ningxia, and placed in charge of the armies of Shanxi, Shaanxi, and Henan.

sentences.zh: 福至鎮，宣布德意，招徠遠人，塞外諸部降者相踵。

translations.literal: When Fu reached his post he proclaimed the court's benevolent intent and drew distant peoples in; tribes beyond the frontier surrendered one after another.
translations.idiomatic: At his post He Fu proclaimed the court's goodwill and drew in distant peoples; tribes beyond the frontier submitted in succession.

sentences.zh: 邊陲無事，因請置驛、屯田、積谷，定賞罰，為經久計。

translations.literal: The frontier was at peace, and he therefore requested post stations, military colonies, grain reserves, and fixed rewards and punishments as a long-term plan.
translations.idiomatic: With the border quiet, he proposed post stations, military colonies, grain reserves, and fixed rules of reward and punishment as a lasting plan.

sentences.zh: 會有讒之者。

translations.literal: There happened to be slanderers.
translations.idiomatic: Slanderers spoke against him.

sentences.zh: 帝不聽，降敕褒慰。

translations.literal: The Emperor would not listen and issued an edict of praise and consolation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor paid no heed and sent an edict praising and reassuring him.

sentences.zh: 永樂五年八月，移鎮甘肅。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the fifth year of Yongle he was transferred to garrison Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Yongle 5 he was transferred to garrison Gansu.

sentences.zh: 福馭軍嚴，下多不便者。

translations.literal: Fu commanded the army strictly, and many under him found it hard to bear.
translations.idiomatic: He Fu ran a tight army, and many of his subordinates resented it.

sentences.zh: 帝間使使戒福，善自衛，毋為小人所中。

translations.literal: The Emperor from time to time sent messengers to warn Fu to guard himself well and not be struck down by petty men.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor now and then sent word warning Fu to look to his own safety and not be undone by petty men.

sentences.zh: 六年，福請遣京師蕃將將迤北降人。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Fu requested that tribal generals from the capital be sent to lead the surrendered northerners.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year He Fu asked that tribal generals from the capital be sent to command the surrendered northerners.

sentences.zh: 帝報曰：「爾久總蕃、漢兵，恐勢眾致讒耳。

translations.literal: The Emperor replied, "You have long commanded both tribal and Han troops; I fear your great strength invites slander.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "You have long commanded both tribal and Han troops; I fear your great strength invites slander.

sentences.zh: 爾老將，朕推誠倚重，毋顧慮。

translations.literal: You are an old general; I rely on you with full sincerity—have no misgivings.
translations.idiomatic: You are an old general; I rely on you with full sincerity—have no misgivings.

sentences.zh: 」尋請以布市馬，選其良者別為群，置官給印專領之。

translations.literal: " Shortly thereafter he requested to trade cloth for horses, select the best and set them apart in separate herds, and appoint officials with seals to oversee them exclusively.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon he proposed trading cloth for horses, selecting the best for separate herds, and appointing officials with seals to oversee them.

sentences.zh: 於是馬大蕃息。

translations.literal: Thereupon horses multiplied greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Horses multiplied greatly as a result.

sentences.zh: 永昌苑牧馬自此始。

translations.literal: Pasturing horses at the Yongchang Park began from this.
translations.idiomatic: Pasturing horses at the Yongchang imperial park began from this.

sentences.zh: 明年，本雅失裏糾阿魯臺將入寇，為瓦剌所敗，走臚朐河，欲收諸部潰卒窺河西。

translations.literal: The next year Benyashiliri rallied Arugtai to invade but was defeated by the Oirats, fled to the Tula River, and wished to gather the scattered troops of various tribes to spy on Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Benyashiri rallied Arugtai for an invasion but was beaten by the Oirats, fled to the Tula River, and tried to rally scattered tribesmen to threaten Hexi.

sentences.zh: 詔福嚴兵為備。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Fu to hold his army in strict readiness.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered He Fu to hold his army in strict readiness.

sentences.zh: 迤北王子、國公、司徒以下十余人帥所部駐亦集乃，乞內附。

translations.literal: More than ten northern princes, state dukes, and situ and below led their followers to encamp at Ejin and begged to submit inward.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten northern princes, state dukes, and situ and below led their followers to camp at Ejin and asked to submit.

sentences.zh: 福以聞，帝令庶子楊榮往，佐福經理，其眾悉降。

translations.literal: Fu reported this; the Emperor ordered Junior Mentor Yang Rong to go and assist Fu in managing affairs, and all their people surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: He Fu reported this; the emperor sent Junior Mentor Yang Rong to assist him, and all their people submitted.

sentences.zh: 福親至亦集乃鎮撫之，送其酋長於京師。

translations.literal: Fu went in person to Ejin to pacify them and sent their chieftains to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He Fu went in person to Ejin to pacify them and sent their chiefs to the capital.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉福功，命榮即軍中封福為寧遠侯，祿千石，且詔福軍中事先行後聞。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised Fu's merit, ordered Rong to enfeoff Fu in the army as Marquis of Ningyuan with an income of one thousand piculs, and also decreed that in military affairs Fu might act first and report afterward.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his service, had Yang Rong enfeoff him in camp as Marquis of Ningyuan with a stipend of one thousand piculs, and decreed that in military affairs he might act first and report afterward.

sentences.zh: 八年，帝北征，召福從出塞。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the Emperor campaigned north and summoned Fu to follow beyond the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year the emperor marched north and summoned He Fu to accompany him beyond the frontier.

sentences.zh: 初，帝以福有才略，寵任逾諸將。

translations.literal: At first the Emperor, because Fu had talent and strategy, favored and entrusted him beyond other generals.
translations.idiomatic: At first the emperor favored He Fu above other generals for his talent and strategic sense.

sentences.zh: 福亦善引嫌，有事未嘗專決。

translations.literal: Fu also knew how to avoid suspicion; when there were matters he never decided alone.
translations.idiomatic: He Fu also knew how to avoid arousing suspicion and never decided important matters on his own.

sentences.zh: 在鎮嘗請取西平侯家鞏昌蓄馬，以充孳牧。

translations.literal: While at his post he once requested to take the horses kept at Gongchang by the Marquis of Xiping's household to replenish breeding herds.
translations.idiomatic: While in command he once asked to take horses kept at Gongchang by the Marquis of Xiping's household to replenish his breeding herds.

sentences.zh: 帝報曰：「皇考時貴近家多許養馬，以示共享富貴之意。

translations.literal: The Emperor replied, "In our late father's time the noble and close families were often allowed to keep horses, to show the meaning of sharing wealth and honor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "In our late father's time the noble and close families were often allowed to keep horses, to show that wealth and honor were to be shared.

sentences.zh: 爾所奏固為國矣，然非待勛戚之道。

translations.literal: What you report is indeed for the state, yet it is not the way to treat meritorious kin.
translations.idiomatic: Your proposal serves the state, but it is not how meritorious kin should be treated.

sentences.zh: 」不聽。

translations.literal: " He did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: " The request was refused.

sentences.zh: 其余有請輒行，委寄甚重。

translations.literal: For other requests he generally acted at once; the trust placed in him was very great.
translations.idiomatic: Other requests he generally carried out at once; the trust placed in him was very great.

sentences.zh: 及從征，數違節度。

translations.literal: When he followed on campaign he repeatedly violated command discipline.
translations.idiomatic: On campaign he repeatedly disobeyed orders.

sentences.zh: 群臣有言其罪者，福益怏怏有怨言。

translations.literal: When ministers spoke of his offenses, Fu grew still more resentful and voiced complaints.
translations.idiomatic: When ministers spoke of his offenses, He Fu grew resentful and voiced complaints.

sentences.zh: 師還，都御史陳瑛復劾之。

translations.literal: When the army returned, Censor-in-chief Chen Ying again impeached him.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, Censor-in-chief Chen Ying impeached him again.

sentences.zh: 福懼，自縊死，爵除。

translations.literal: Fu was afraid and hanged himself; his title was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: He Fu, in fear, hanged himself, and his title was abolished.

sentences.zh: 而趙王妃亦尋廢。

translations.literal: The Princess of Zhao was also soon deposed.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Zhao was soon deposed as well.

sentences.zh: 顧成，字景韶，其先湘潭人。

translations.literal: Gu Cheng, courtesy name Jingshao, his ancestors were natives of Xiangtan.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Cheng, courtesy name Jingshao, came of a family originally from Xiangtan.

sentences.zh: 祖父業操舟，往來江、淮間，遂家江都。

translations.literal: His grandfather Ye worked boats, traveling between the Yangzi and Huai, and settled the family at Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ye was a boatman on the Yangzi and Huai routes and eventually settled the family at Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 成少魁岸，膂力絕人，善馬槊，文其身以自異。

translations.literal: Cheng in youth was tall and imposing, with strength beyond other men; skilled with the cavalry lance, he tattooed his body to set himself apart.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Gu Cheng was tall and imposing, with extraordinary strength; skilled with the cavalry lance, he tattooed his body to set himself apart.

sentences.zh: 太祖渡江，來歸，以勇選為帳前親兵，擎蓋出入。

translations.literal: When the founding emperor crossed the Yangzi, he came over in submission; for his valor he was chosen as a personal guard before the tent, bearing the canopy in and out.
translations.idiomatic: When the founding emperor crossed the Yangzi, he came over in submission; for his valor he was chosen as a personal guard and bore the imperial canopy on campaign.

sentences.zh: 嘗從上出，舟膠於沙，成負舟而行。

translations.literal: Once when he followed the emperor out, the boat stuck on sand; Cheng carried the boat on his back and walked.
translations.idiomatic: Once when he accompanied the emperor, the boat ran aground; Gu Cheng shouldered it and carried it forward.

sentences.zh: 從攻鎮江，與勇士十人轉鬥入城，被執，十人皆死。

translations.literal: He followed in the attack on Zhenjiang; with ten brave men he fought his way into the city, was captured, and the ten all died.
translations.idiomatic: At the attack on Zhenjiang he fought his way into the city with ten brave men, was captured, and all ten companions were killed.

sentences.zh: 成躍起斷縛，仆持刀者，脫歸。

translations.literal: Cheng leaped up, broke his bonds, threw down the man with the blade, and escaped back.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Cheng leaped up, broke his bonds, knocked down the man with the blade, and escaped.

sentences.zh: 導眾攻城，克之，授百戶。

translations.literal: He led the troops in storming the city and took it; he was appointed centurion.
translations.idiomatic: He led the assault, took the city, and was appointed centurion.

sentences.zh: 大小數十戰，皆有功，進堅城衛指揮僉事。

translations.literal: In several dozen battles large and small he had merit each time and was advanced to Assistant Commander of the Jiancheng Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In dozens of battles large and small he distinguished himself and was promoted to assistant commander of the Jiancheng Guard.

sentences.zh: 從伐蜀，攻羅江，擒元帥以下二十余人，進降漢州。

translations.literal: He followed the Shu campaign, attacked Luojiang, captured the yuanshuai and more than twenty others below him, and advanced to accept the surrender of Hanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He marched on Shu, attacked Luojiang, captured the Yuan commander and more than twenty officers under him, and advanced to accept Hanzhou's surrender.

sentences.zh: 蜀平，改成都後衛。

translations.literal: When Shu was pacified he was transferred to the Rear Chengdu Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Shu was pacified he was transferred to the Rear Chengdu Guard.

sentences.zh: 洪武六年，擒重慶妖賊王元保。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Hongwu he captured the Chongqing sorcerer-rebel Wang Yuanbao.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 6 he captured the Chongqing rebel sorcerer Wang Yuanbao.

sentences.zh: 八年調守貴州。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred to garrison Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was transferred to garrison Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 時群蠻叛服不常，成連歲出兵，悉平之。

translations.literal: At that time the tribal peoples submitted and rebelled without constancy; Cheng campaigned year after year and pacified them all.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes submitted and rebelled by turns; Gu Cheng campaigned year after year until all were pacified.

sentences.zh: 已，從潁川侯傅友德征雲南，為前鋒，首克普定，留成列柵以守。

translations.literal: Before long he followed Marquis of Yingchuan Fu Youde in the Yunnan campaign as vanguard, first taking Puding; Cheng was left to set up stockades and hold it.
translations.idiomatic: He then followed Marquis of Yingchuan Fu Youde against Yunnan as vanguard, was first to take Puding, and was left there to build stockades and hold the place.

sentences.zh: 蠻數萬來攻，成出柵，手殺數十百人，賊退走。

translations.literal: Tens of thousands of tribesmen came to attack; Cheng went out of the stockade and with his own hand killed several hundred men, and the rebels retreated.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands of tribesmen attacked; Gu Cheng sallied from the stockade and killed several hundred with his own hand, and the rebels fled.

sentences.zh: 余賊猶在南城，成斬所俘而縱其一，曰：「吾夜二鼓來殺汝。

translations.literal: The remaining rebels were still in the south city; Cheng beheaded the prisoners and released one, saying, "At the second watch tonight I shall come to kill you.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining rebels held the south city; Gu Cheng beheaded the prisoners but released one, telling him, "At the second watch tonight I shall come to kill you.

sentences.zh: 」夜二鼓，吹角鳴炮，賊聞悉走，獲器甲無算。

translations.literal: " At the second watch of the night he sounded horns and fired cannon; hearing this, the rebels all fled, and weapons and armor captured were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: " At the second watch he sounded horns and fired cannon; the rebels fled at the noise, and the arms and armor captured were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 進指揮使。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to commander.

sentences.zh: 諸蠻隸普定者悉平。

translations.literal: All tribes subject to Puding were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: All tribes under Puding were pacified.

sentences.zh: 十七年，平阿黑、螺螄等十余寨。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he pacified Ahei, Luosi, and more than ten stockades.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he pacified Ahei, Luosi, and more than ten stockades.

sentences.zh: 明年奏罷普定府，析其地為三州、六長官司。

translations.literal: The next year he memorialized to abolish the Puding prefecture and divide its territory into three prefectures and six native offices.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he memorialized to abolish Puding Prefecture and divide its territory into three prefectures and six native offices.

sentences.zh: 進貴州都指揮同知。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Vice Commander of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice commander of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 有告其受賕及僭用玉器等物者，以久勞不問。

translations.literal: Someone reported that he had accepted bribes and presumptuously used jade vessels and the like; because of his long service he was not questioned.
translations.idiomatic: He was accused of taking bribes and using jade vessels reserved for the throne, but because of his long service the charges were not pursued.

sentences.zh: 二十九年遷右軍都督僉事，佩征南將軍印。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he was transferred to Vice Commissioner-in-chief of the Right Army and wore the seal of General for the Southern Campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year he was made vice commissioner-in-chief of the Right Army and given the seal of General for the Southern Campaign.

sentences.zh: 會何福討水西蠻，斬其酋居宗必登。

translations.literal: It happened that He Fu campaigned against the Shuixi tribes and beheaded the chieftain Juzong Bideng.
translations.idiomatic: When He Fu campaigned against the Shuixi tribes, Gu Cheng beheaded the chieftain Juzong Bideng.

sentences.zh: 明年，西堡、滄浪諸寨蠻亂，成遣指揮陸秉與其子統分道討平之。

translations.literal: The next year the tribes of Xibao, Canglang, and other stockades rebelled; Cheng sent Commander Lu Bing and his son Tong by separate routes to pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the tribes of Xibao, Canglang, and other stockades rebelled; he sent Commander Lu Bing and his son Tong by separate routes to put them down.

sentences.zh: 成在貴州凡十余年，討平諸苗洞寨以百數，皆誅其渠魁，撫綏余眾。

translations.literal: Cheng was in Guizhou for more than ten years in all, pacifying several hundred Miao cave-stockades; in each case he executed the ringleaders and soothed the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Cheng spent more than ten years in Guizhou, pacifying several hundred Miao stockades; he executed the ringleaders in each case and soothed the rest.

sentences.zh: 恩信大布，蠻人帖服。

translations.literal: His kindness and trust were widely spread, and the tribes submitted.
translations.idiomatic: His kindness and authority spread far, and the tribes submitted.

sentences.zh: 是年二月，召還京。

translations.literal: In the second month of that year he was summoned back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: That year, in the second month, he was recalled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 成性忠謹，涉獵書史。

translations.literal: Cheng's nature was loyal and careful; he dipped into books and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Cheng was loyal and conscientious and read widely in books and histories.

sentences.zh: 始居北平，多效謀畫，然終不肯將兵，賜兵器亦不受。

translations.literal: When he first lived at Beiping he often offered plans, yet he would never command troops in the end, and weapons bestowed on him he also would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: When he first lived at Beiping he often offered strategic advice, yet he refused to command troops and would not accept weapons bestowed on him.

sentences.zh: 再鎮貴州，屢平播州、都勻諸叛蠻，威鎮南中，土人立生祠祀焉。

translations.literal: Garrisoning Guizhou again, he repeatedly pacified the rebel tribes of Bozhou, Duyun, and others; his authority awed the south, and the local people erected living shrines to worship him.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned to Guizhou he repeatedly pacified rebel tribes in Bozhou, Duyun, and elsewhere; his authority awed the south, and the local people built living shrines in his honor.

sentences.zh: 其被召至京也，命輔太子監國。

translations.literal: When he was summoned to the capital he was ordered to assist the crown prince in overseeing the state.
translations.idiomatic: When he was summoned to the capital he was ordered to assist the crown prince in overseeing the state.

sentences.zh: 成頓首言：「太子仁明，廷臣皆賢，輔導之事非愚臣所及，請歸備蠻。

translations.literal: Cheng bowed his head and said, "The crown prince is benevolent and bright, and the court ministers are all worthy; guidance is beyond this foolish subject's capacity—I beg to return and guard against the tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Cheng kowtowed and said, "The crown prince is benevolent and wise, and the court ministers are all capable; guidance is beyond this humble servant—I beg to return to guard the frontier against the tribes.

sentences.zh: 」時群小謀奪嫡，太子不自安。

translations.literal: " At that time petty men plotted to seize the succession, and the crown prince was ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: " Petty men at court were plotting to displace him, and the crown prince was ill at ease.

sentences.zh: 成入辭文華殿，因曰：「殿下但當竭誠孝敬，孳孳恤民。

translations.literal: Cheng entered the Wenhua Hall to take leave and said, "Your Highness need only exhaust sincerity in filial devotion and labor constantly in caring for the people.
translations.idiomatic: Taking leave in the Wenhua Hall, he told the prince, "Your Highness need only serve your father with complete devotion and labor constantly for the people's welfare.

sentences.zh: 萬事在天，小人不足措意。

translations.literal: All affairs rest with Heaven; petty men are not worth a thought.
translations.idiomatic: All else rests with Heaven; petty men are not worth troubling over.

sentences.zh: 」十二年五月卒，年八十有五。

translations.literal: " In the fifth month of the twelfth year he died, aged eighty-five.
translations.idiomatic: " He died in the fifth month of the twelfth year, at the age of eighty-five.

sentences.zh: 贈夏國公，謚武毅。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Xia with the posthumous title Wuyi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Xia with the posthumous title Wuyi.

sentences.zh: 八子。

translations.literal: He had eight sons.
translations.idiomatic: He had eight sons.

sentences.zh: 長統，普定衛指揮，以成降燕被誅。

translations.literal: The eldest, Tong, was commander of the Puding Guard; because Cheng surrendered to Yan he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest, Tong, was commander of the Puding Guard; because Gu Cheng had surrendered to Yan, he was executed.

sentences.zh: 從弟溥嗣，掌五軍右掖。

translations.literal: His younger cousin Pu succeeded him and held the right wing of the Five Armies.
translations.idiomatic: His younger cousin Pu succeeded him and held the right wing of the Five Armies.

sentences.zh: 弘治二年，拜平蠻將軍，鎮湖廣。

translations.literal: In the second year of Hongzhi he was appointed General for the Pacification of the Tribes and garrisoned Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi 2 he was named General for the Pacification of the Tribes and posted to Huguang.

sentences.zh: 始至，捕斬苗中首惡。

translations.literal: When he first arrived he captured and beheaded the chief evildoers among the Miao.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he captured and executed the worst offenders among the Miao.

sentences.zh: 五年十月，貴州都勻苗乜富架作亂，自稱都順王，梗滇、蜀道。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the fifth year the Duyun Miao chieftain Yefujia rebelled in Guizhou, styled himself King of Dushun, and blocked the roads to Yunnan and Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the fifth year the Duyun Miao chieftain Yefujia rebelled in Guizhou, proclaimed himself King of Dushun, and blocked the roads to Yunnan and Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 詔溥充總兵官，帥兵八萬討之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Pu to serve as overall commander and lead eighty thousand troops against him.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Pu to take supreme command and lead eighty thousand troops against him.

sentences.zh: 分五路刻期並進，誅富架父子，斬首萬計。

translations.literal: He divided into five routes with a fixed date to advance together, executed Yefujia and his son, and heads cut numbered on the order of ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He divided his force into five columns that advanced on a fixed date, executed Yefujia and his son, and took tens of thousands of heads.

sentences.zh: 加太子太保，增祿二百石。

translations.literal: He was made Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and his stipend was increased by two hundred piculs.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and his stipend was increased by two hundred piculs.

sentences.zh: 召入提督團營，掌前軍都督府事。

translations.literal: He was summoned in to supervise the training corps and manage affairs of the Front Army Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to supervise the training corps and manage the Front Army Commission.

sentences.zh: 十六年，卒。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he died.

sentences.zh: 謚襄恪。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Xiangke.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous title Xiangke.

sentences.zh: 溥清慎守法，卒之日，囊無余資，英國公張懋出布帛以斂。

translations.literal: Pu was pure, careful, and law-abiding; on the day he died his purse held no surplus, and Duke of Ying Zhang Mao provided cloth and silk for the burial.
translations.idiomatic: Pu was pure, careful, and law-abiding; when he died his purse was empty, and Duke of Ying Zhang Mao provided cloth and silk for his burial.

sentences.zh: 子仕隆嗣，管神機營左哨，得士心。

translations.literal: His son Shilong succeeded him, commanded the left wing of the Divine Engine Corps, and won the soldiers' hearts.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shilong succeeded him, commanded the left wing of the Divine Engine Corps, and won the soldiers' loyalty.

sentences.zh: 正德初，出為漕運總兵，數請恤軍卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengde he went out as overall commander of grain transport and repeatedly requested relief for the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhengde reign he was posted as overall commander of grain transport and repeatedly petitioned for relief for his troops.

sentences.zh: 鎮淮安十余年，以清白聞。

translations.literal: He garrisoned Huaian for more than ten years and was known for integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted at Huaian for more than ten years and was known for integrity.

sentences.zh: 武宗南巡，江彬橫甚，折辱諸大吏，惟仕隆不為屈。

translations.literal: When Wuzong toured the south, Jiang Bin was extremely overbearing and humiliated the great officials; only Shilong would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wuzong emperor toured the south, Jiang Bin bullied the high officials shamelessly; only Shilong would not bow to him.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，移鎮湖廣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiajing he was transferred to garrison Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jiajing reign he was transferred to Huguang.

sentences.zh: 尋召還，論奉迎防守功。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was recalled and his merit was assessed for welcoming the emperor and holding the defense.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled and rewarded for his service in welcoming the new emperor and holding the defense.

sentences.zh: 加太子太傅，掌中軍都督府事。

translations.literal: He was made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and managed affairs of the Central Army Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and put in charge of the Central Army Commission.

sentences.zh: 錦衣千戶王邦奇者，怨大學士楊廷和、兵部尚書彭澤，上疏言：「哈密失策，事由兩人。

translations.literal: Wang Bangqi, a chiliarch of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, bore resentment against Grand Secretary Yang Tinghe and Minister of War Peng Ze and submitted a memorial saying, "The Hami blunder arose from these two men.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bangqi, a chiliarch of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, hated Grand Secretary Yang Tinghe and Minister of War Peng Ze and memorialized the throne: "The Hami disaster was their doing.

sentences.zh: 」帝怒，逮系廷和諸子婿。

translations.literal: " The Emperor was angry and arrested Yang Tinghe's sons and sons-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was furious and arrested Yang Tinghe's sons and sons-in-law.

sentences.zh: 給事中楊言疏救，忤旨。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Yang Yan memorialized in their defense and offended the imperial will.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Yang Yan memorialized in their defense and offended the emperor.

sentences.zh: 事下五府九卿科道議，仕隆言：「廷和功在社稷。

translations.literal: The matter was sent down for discussion by the five commissions, nine ministers, and censorial officials; Shilong said, "Tinghe's merit lies with the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was referred to the five commissions, nine ministers, and censorial officials; Shilong said, "Yang Tinghe's service to the state is beyond question.

sentences.zh: 邦奇小人，假邊事惑聖聽，傷國體。

translations.literal: Bangqi is a petty man who uses frontier affairs to mislead the sacred ear and harm the dignity of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Bangqi is a petty man who uses frontier affairs to mislead the throne and harm the dignity of the state.

sentences.zh: 」有詔切責，移病解營務。

translations.literal: " An edict sharply rebuked him; he pleaded illness and resigned his camp duties.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict sharply rebuked him; he pleaded illness and resigned his post.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 贈太傅，謚榮靖。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Preceptor with the posthumous title Rongjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Preceptor with the posthumous title Rongjing.

sentences.zh: 子寰嗣，守備南京。

translations.literal: His son Huan succeeded him and served as garrison commander of Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: His son Huan succeeded him and served as garrison commander of Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 奉詔讞獄，多所平反。

translations.literal: By imperial order he reviewed cases in prison and reversed many wrongful judgments.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial order he reviewed prison cases and reversed many wrongful convictions.

sentences.zh: 十七年為漕運總兵官。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he became overall commander of grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he became overall commander of grain transport.

sentences.zh: 明年，獻皇后梓宮赴承天，漕舟以避梓宮後期者三千。

translations.literal: The next year, when Empress Xian's coffin went to Chengtian, three thousand grain boats were late because they yielded to the coffin procession.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, when Empress Xian's coffin was sent to Chengtian, three thousand grain boats fell behind because they had to yield to the funeral procession.

sentences.zh: 而江南北多災傷，寰請被災地停漕一年，令改折色，軍民交便。

translations.literal: Meanwhile north and south of the Yangzi there were many disasters; Huan requested that grain transport be halted for one year in the afflicted areas and commutation to cash payments ordered, to the mutual convenience of army and people.
translations.idiomatic: Disasters had struck both north and south of the Yangzi; Huan asked that grain transport be suspended for a year in the affected areas and commuted to cash payments, to the benefit of troops and civilians alike.

sentences.zh: 又條上漕政七事，並施行。

translations.literal: He also submitted seven items on grain-transport policy in detail, and all were put into effect.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted seven proposals for reforming grain transport, all of which were adopted.

sentences.zh: 諸為漕蠹者病之，遂布蜚語，為給事中王交所劾。

translations.literal: Those who profited from abuses in grain transport resented this and spread slander; he was impeached by Supervising Secretary Wang Jiao.
translations.idiomatic: Those who profited from abuses in the transport system resented him and spread rumors; Supervising Secretary Wang Jiao impeached him.

sentences.zh: 已，按驗不實，再鎮淮安。

translations.literal: Before long investigation found the charges untrue, and he was again posted at Huaian.
translations.idiomatic: Investigation proved the charges false, and he was posted again at Huaian.

sentences.zh: 會安南事起，移鎮兩廣。

translations.literal: When the Annam affair arose he was transferred to garrison the two Guang provinces.
translations.idiomatic: When trouble broke out in Annam he was transferred to the two Guang provinces.

sentences.zh: 莫宏瀷者，安南都統使莫福海子也。

translations.literal: Mo Hongyan was the son of Mo Fuhai, Commissioner-in-chief of Annam.
translations.idiomatic: Mo Hongyan was the son of Mo Fuhai, the commissioner-in-chief of Annam.

sentences.zh: 福海死，宏瀷幼。

translations.literal: Fuhai died while Hongyan was still young.
translations.idiomatic: When Fuhai died, Hongyan was still a child.

sentences.zh: 其權臣阮敬與族人莫正中構兵，國內亂，正中逃入欽州。

translations.literal: The powerful minister Ruan Jing and his clansman Mo Zhengzhong raised troops in conflict; the country fell into civil strife, and Zhengzhong fled into Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The powerful minister Ruan Jing and his clansman Mo Zhengzhong raised troops against each other; civil war broke out, and Zhengzhong fled into Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 時有議乘釁取安南者，寰與提督侍郎周延決策，請於朝，令宏瀷襲都統使，安南遂定。

translations.literal: At the time some argued to seize the opportunity and take Annam; Huan and the supervising vice minister Zhou Yan decided otherwise, petitioned the court, and had Hongyan succeed as commissioner-in-chief, and Annam was thus settled.
translations.idiomatic: Some at court urged seizing the opportunity to conquer Annam; Huan and supervising vice minister Zhou Yan decided otherwise, petitioned the throne to confirm Hongyan as commissioner-in-chief, and Annam was stabilized.

sentences.zh: 三十年事也。

translations.literal: This was in the thirtieth year.
translations.idiomatic: This was in the thirtieth year.

sentences.zh: 尋以兵討平桂林、平樂叛瑤。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter with troops he campaigned and pacified the rebel Yao of Guilin and Pingle.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he campaigned and pacified the rebel Yao of Guilin and Pingle.

sentences.zh: 復命鎮淮，有禦倭功。

translations.literal: He was again ordered to garrison the Huai region and had merit in repelling the Japanese pirates.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted again to the Huai region and distinguished himself against the wokou pirates.

sentences.zh: 入總京營，加太子太保。

translations.literal: He entered the capital to take overall command of the metropolitan camps and was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to command the metropolitan camps and made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 復出督漕。

translations.literal: He again went out to supervise grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out again to supervise grain transport.

sentences.zh: 召還。

translations.literal: He was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled.

sentences.zh: 請老。

translations.literal: He requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: He requested retirement.

sentences.zh: 隆慶五年，特起授京營總督。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Longqing he was specially recalled and appointed governor of the metropolitan camps.
translations.idiomatic: In Longqing 5 he was specially recalled and appointed governor of the metropolitan camps.

sentences.zh: 尋乞休。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he begged to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 神宗嗣位，起掌左府。

translations.literal: When Shenzong succeeded to the throne he was raised to manage the Left Commission.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wanli emperor succeeded, he was recalled to manage the Left Army Commission.

sentences.zh: 久之，致仕。

translations.literal: After a long time he retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time he retired from office.

sentences.zh: 加少保。

translations.literal: He was made Junior Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Junior Guardian.

sentences.zh: 萬歷九年卒。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Wanli he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Wanli 9.

sentences.zh: 贈太傅，謚榮僖。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Preceptor with the posthumous title Rongxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Preceptor with the posthumous title Rongxi.

sentences.zh: 自溥至寰三世，皆寬和廉靖，內行飭謹，曉文藝。

translations.literal: From Pu to Huan across three generations, all were mild, honest, and upright in conduct, strict in private behavior, and versed in letters and arts.
translations.idiomatic: From Pu through Huan, three generations were mild, honest, and upright, strict in private conduct, and accomplished in letters and the arts.

sentences.zh: 仕隆、寰兩世督漕，皆勤於職。

translations.literal: Shilong and Huan for two generations supervised grain transport and were both diligent in duty.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong and Huan for two generations supervised grain transport, and both were diligent in their duties.

sentences.zh: 三傳至孫肇跡，京師陷，死於賊。

translations.literal: After three transmissions the line reached the grandson Zhao Ji; when the capital fell he died at the hands of the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Three generations later the line reached the grandson Zhao Ji; when the capital fell he died at the hands of the rebels.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：東昌、小河之戰，盛庸、平安屢挫燕師，斬其驍將，厥功甚壯。

translations.literal: The commentator says: At the battles of Dongchang and the Xiao River, Sheng Yong and Ping An repeatedly checked the Yan army and slew their fierce generals—their achievement was very grand.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: At Dongchang and the Xiao River, Sheng Yong and Ping An repeatedly turned back the Yan army and killed their boldest commanders—an achievement of real stature.

sentences.zh: 及至兵敗被執，不克引義自裁，隱忍偷生，視鐵鉉、暴昭輩，能無愧乎？

translations.literal: Yet when at last they were defeated and captured, they could not take righteousness and cut themselves down, but endured in shame to cling to life—compared with Tie Xian, Bao Zhao, and their kind, can they be without shame?
translations.idiomatic: Yet when they were defeated and captured they could not die for principle but clung to life in shame—how can they face Tie Xian, Bao Zhao, and men like them without shame?

sentences.zh: 何福、顧成皆太祖時宿將，著功邊僥。

translations.literal: He Fu and Gu Cheng were both veteran generals of the founding emperor's time who achieved distinction on the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: He Fu and Gu Cheng were both veteran generals of the founding reign who won distinction on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 而一遇燕兵，或引卻南奔，或身遭俘馘。

translations.literal: Yet once they met the Yan army, one drew back and fled south, the other was himself captured.
translations.idiomatic: Yet once they met the Yan army, one retreated south in flight, the other was taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 成祖棄瑕錄舊，均列茅土，亦雲幸矣。

translations.literal: Chengzu overlooked their flaws and recorded their old service, enfeoffing them all alike—they were fortunate indeed.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongle Emperor overlooked their flaws for old service's sake and enfeoffed them all alike—they were fortunate indeed.

sentences.zh: 福固不以功名終，而成之延及苗裔，榮不勝辱，亦奚足取哉。

translations.literal: Fu indeed did not end in fame and success, yet Cheng's line extended to later generations—when honor cannot overcome disgrace, what is there worth taking?
translations.idiomatic: Fu did not end in glory, yet Cheng's line extended to later generations—when honor cannot outweigh disgrace, what is there to admire?
